newsitem.title: FRANCE: PSA confident on sales outside Europe.
newsitem.headline: PSA confident on sales outside Europe.

text.p: PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman Jacques Calvet said on Wednesday he was confident the French company would meet its target of selling 25 percent of its cars outside western Europe by the year 2000.
"We are confident of realising this objective," he told a news conference, citing progress on production projects outside Europe and higher exports outside the region, particularly to eastern Europe.
Currently the group sells 13 percent of its vehicles outside western Europe.
Calvet said a joint venture in Malaysia with Proton was expected to produce 10,000 Tiara cars in 1996, its first year, and double that amount in 1997.

He said the Chinese operation was suffering from the government's anti-inflation drive that had squeezed liquidity. The PSA group recently said it was studying concentrating its Chinese production, currently at two plants, at the modern Citroen plant in the central Chinese city of Wuhan.
Production at the Wuhan plant -- currently 48 vehicles a day -- should rise by 12 cars daily each month beginning in February, Calvet said.
Production is expected to rise to 25,000 next year from 9,500 this year, he said.
"We are in the process of establishing a modern dealer network, perhaps the first in China," he said. It would include 100 dealers and four regional offices.
PSA officials said they expected the Chinese market next year to total between 200,000 and 220,000 cars.
Calvet said the group was preparing for the eventual production in Uruguay of 12,000 cars for export in the Mercosur trade zone. This year it began producing 306 cars in Argentina.

He said the group's interest in establishing a strong presence in the Mercosur zone, grouping Uruguay, Paraguay, Argentina and Brazil, had led it to push back considerations of setting up car production in the United States.

Calvet said the group was still in discussions with several Brazilian states with a view to setting up production there. "We expect to make a decision soon," he said. "We're making progress in Brazil."
He said the group had "contacts" with Russia but no precise project.
